chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know why Al-Ta'if has been named so?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) supplicated to his Lord that He should grant his family from the fruits, He cut off for them a piece from the earth, so it came forward until it performed Tawaf by the House (Kaaba) seven (circuits). Then Allah settled it in its place. And indeed, Al-Ta'if was named so due to the Tawaf by the House.'

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيم: Ibrahim (Prophet Abraham, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الطَّائِف: Al-Ta'if (the name of the city, literally meaning 'the one that circulates/moves')
key_terms.الْبَيْت: Al-Bayt (The House, referring to the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the name Al-Ta'if according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi offers a unique cosmological etymology for 'Al-Ta'if', linking the city's name to the miraculous circumambulation (Tawaf) of a land fragment by Prophet Ibrahim (AS). It highlights the deep spiritual connection between the Kaaba and surrounding geography, framing Ta'if not merely as a settlement but as a participant in the sacred rites of Mecca. This perspective reinforces the sanctity of the region within Shia exegetical traditions, viewing physical locations as active witnesses to prophetic history.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘Do you know why Al-Ta’if has been named so?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘When Ibrahimas supplicated to hisas Lordazwj that Heazwj should Grace hisas family from the fruits, Heazwj Cut-off a piece of land for them, from the Jordan. So it came over until it performed Tawaaf by the House (Kaaba), seven (circuits). Then Allahazwj Settled it in its place. And rather, Al-Ta’if was named so due to the Tawaaf of the House (Kaaba)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who has said the following: “Once abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked me, ‘Why is the name al-Ta’if?’ I (the narrator) replied, ‘No, I do not know.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘When Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, prayed to his Lord to provide his family with sustenance, Allah cut a piece of land from ’ Adan (a mountain in al-Sham). It came and performed Tawaf around the House seven times then Allah set it in its place and it is called al-Ta’if because of its performing Tawaf around the House.’”
